transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Uh, yeah… I guess I’m here because my eating’s been kind of out of control lately. Like I’ll get off a long shift, or if I’ve been studying—well, trying to study, I didn’t exactly love school the first time around, but I’m trying to get some certifications—and then I’ll just eat way more than I meant to.

Like, it’ll be a whole fast-food meal, then snacks, then I’m still going through whatever’s in the fridge, all in one sitting. I tell myself I’m just hungry from work, but it feels like… more than that, I guess.
When you find yourself eating more than you meant to, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating once you start?

Yeah… yeah, that’s pretty much what it feels like. Like once I start on those nights, my brain’s saying, “Okay, stop, you’re full,” but my hands just keep grabbing stuff anyway. And I’ll already be feeling kind of sick, like my stomach’s telling me I overdid it, but I still keep going.

It’s weird because at work I can control myself fine, you know, like with tools and engines and all that, but then with food it’s like I just… don’t hit the brakes.
After these episodes where you feel like you can't control your eating, do you ever make yourself sick or exercise a lot to try to get rid of the calories you consumed?

Yeah… sometimes. I mean, not every single time, but after I really overdo it, I’ll go to the bathroom and make myself throw up.

It’s embarrassing to say. Like, I’ll be thinking about how much I ate and what it’s going to do to me, and then I kind of panic. Sometimes I’ve taken laxatives too, for the same reason. I know it probably sounds stupid—my buddy at the shop is always joking about “burning off lunch” when we’re hauling parts around, but this isn’t really like that. It’s more like I’m trying to undo what I just did.
How often do these episodes happen, and do they bother you or affect things like your work or relationships?

Most weeks… yeah, I’d say there’s at least one night where it happens. Like I’ll eat way too much and then I’m trying to fix it after—throwing up, or sometimes laxatives, or I’ll skip eating the next day or work out extra.

It’s been going on for several months now. I kept telling myself it was just stress, or long shifts, you know—being around diesel fumes all day and then coming home wiped out, it’s easy to just grab food and not think. But yeah, it bothers me. I don’t really like people noticing, so I kind of keep it to myself, and that makes it awkward sometimes.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports recurrent episodes of eating significantly more than intended, feeling a lack of control during these episodes, and engaging in compensatory behaviors such as self-induced vomiting and laxative use. These behaviors occur at least once a week and have been ongoing for several months. This presentation aligns with binge eating followed by inappropriate compensatory behavior, which is characteristic of F50.2 (Binge Eating Disorder with compensatory behaviors). Other eating disorder diagnoses (F50.0, F50.1, F50.9) are ruled out based on current symptom presentation.
